title: Макс съедает отравленное блюдо  (Max Eats the Spiked Dish)

segments.t: When the spiked complimentary dish is returned from the dining room untouched, an unsuspecting Max grabs the plate in the kitchen and eats the entire portion himself. Moments later, while Barinov waits eagerly for the goalkeeper's stomach to cramp up, Max doubles over on the kitchen floor screaming for an ambulance.

'Do not worry so much.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'not' and finishing on 'like this'. Lyova answers right away.
'He will start running even faster.' The meaning hinges on 'he' working together with 'will start' in spoken Russian.

'You may take away my masterpiece, Alexandra.' Max anchors the line on 'you', while 'Alexander' completes the thought.
'With pleasure.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'with', while 'pleasure' completes the thought. Lyova answers right away.
'Listen, we need to remake this.' In Russian, the idea of 'listen' flows naturally into 'to redo' without extra filler words.
'It tastes kind of sour.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'kind of' before landing on 'sour'.
'Well, how is it going?' Notice how Russian expresses 'come on' and 'what' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Lyova answers right away.
'Any second now.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'any minute' and finishing on 'any minute'.

'Well, his stomach will cramp up.' Notice how Russian expresses 'come on' and 'twist' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
